title: 21 Million Viewers and a Sky Full of Fire: House of the Dragon Season 3 Is Here — and India Is Watching in Real Time
excerpt: The Battle of the Gullet opened the bloodiest chapter in Westeros history. Episode 2 drops tonight. And for the first time, Indian audiences don't have to wait a single second.
body:
The dragons are back. And this time, they brought carnage.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=0JlMjgqduVw</youtube>

**House of the Dragon** returned on June 21 with a Season 3 premiere that showrunner **Ryan Condal** called "arguably the craziest episode of television ever made" — and 21.5 million viewers worldwide showed up in the first three days to find out if he was right. He was.

The premiere plunged audiences straight into the **Battle of the Gullet**, the bloodiest naval engagement in Westeros history. Ships burned. Dragons screamed. Major characters died. There was no slow build, no political table-setting — just fire, blood, and the kind of spectacle that reminds you why HBO still owns prestige television when it decides to stop holding back.

## What Happened in the Premiere

Without spoiling every beat: the battle that Season 2's divisive finale promised has finally arrived. **Rhaenyra's** (Emma D'Arcy) forces and **Aegon's** (Tom Glynn-Carney) Green faction collided at sea in a sequence that combined practical effects, jaw-dropping VFX, and genuine emotional stakes. **Aemond Targaryen** (Ewan Mitchell) continued his transformation into the most terrifying character on television, while **Daemon** (Matt Smith) did what Daemon always does — looked magnificent and made questionable decisions.

The critical response has been overwhelmingly positive. After a Season 2 that divided fans with its slow pacing and abrupt finale, Season 3 seems to have course-corrected with a vengeance.



> **"But here's what that framing misses: 21.5 million viewers for any show in 2026 is extraordinary."**


> "The pace quickens, the characters start using their brains, and there's even a smidgen of levity mixed in with all the heads on pikes and grieving mothers."

## The Numbers Tell a Story

Those 21.5 million viewers represent an 8% drop from Season 2's premiere (23.4 million), and the entertainment press has had a field day with the decline narrative. But here's what that framing misses: 21.5 million viewers for any show in 2026 is extraordinary. This isn't a ratings disaster — it's a show that shed some of the tourists who checked out after Season 2's finale and retained its devoted base.

Warner Bros. Discovery also noted that Season 2 viewership *tripled* in the weeks before the Season 3 premiere, suggesting a massive rewatch wave that likely converted new viewers along the way.

## Episode 2 Drops Tonight

New episodes air every Sunday at 9 PM ET on **HBO** and **HBO Max**, with eight episodes running through August 9. Episode 2 arrives tonight (June 28), and based on the premiere's momentum, the table is set for what could be the show's strongest season yet.

The full episode schedule:
- **Episode 2:** June 28
- **Episode 3:** July 5
- **Episode 4:** July 12
- **Episode 5:** July 19
- **Episode 6:** July 26
- **Episode 7:** August 2
- **Episode 8 (Finale):** August 9

## Where to Watch in India — No Waiting Required

This is where it matters for diaspora audiences: **House of the Dragon Season 3 is streaming simultaneously on JioHotstar** in India, available in **English, Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu**. No delays. No geo-restrictions. No waiting for a separate Indian premiere window.

For NRIs in the US, the show is on **HBO Max** (plans start at $10.99/month with ads, $18.49 ad-free). In the UK, it's on **Sky Atlantic** and **NOW TV**. Canadian viewers can catch it on **Crave**.

The simultaneous global release means Indian viewers can participate in the weekly conversation — the theories, the memes, the collective gasps — without being a day behind. For a franchise built on water-cooler moments, that matters.

## The Cast to Watch

Season 3 brings back the full ensemble: **Matt Smith** as Daemon, **Emma D'Arcy** as Rhaenyra, **Olivia Cooke** as Alicent, **Ewan Mitchell** as the increasingly unhinged Aemond, **Tom Glynn-Carney** as King Aegon II, **Rhys Ifans** as Otto Hightower, and **Steve Toussaint** as Lord Corlys Velaryon. **Abigail Thorn** joins as Admiral Sharako Lohar, adding a new dimension to the already stacked roster.

If the premiere is any indication, this season isn't interested in making you wait for the spectacle. The Targaryens are at war. The dragons are in the air. And 21 million people — including a growing Indian audience streaming in four languages — are watching it burn.
